# North Korea revises constitution to drop references to unification of Korean Peninsula

By Kyu-Seok Shim

May 6, 2026 6:36 AM UTC Updated May 6, 2026

- North Korea revises constitution to define its territory as bordering South Korea
- New constitution does not include references to unification
- Revised document strengthens and codifies leader Kim's nuclear role

SEOUL, May 6 (Reuters) - North Korea has revised its constitution to define its territory ‌as bordering South Korea and remove references to reunification, according to a draft of the text reviewed by Reuters, codifying leader Kim Jong Un’s push to treat the two Koreas as separate states.
